Desolder a two-lead part without overhea.check_prompt: Why add fresh solder before desoldering?
Desolder a two-lead part without overhea.criterion: Fresh solder and alternating heat keep the part and the pads alive.
Desolder a two-lead part without overhea.explanation: Old solder has lost its flux, so adding fresh solder is what makes removal quick.
Desolder a two-lead part without overhea.practice: Add fresh solder to each joint, alternate heat between the leads, and pull gently once both are molten.

Form a lead so the part seats flush.check_prompt: Which side of the board should the bent lead sit on?
Form a lead so the part seats flush.criterion: The body sits flat with the lead bent between the body and the pad.
Form a lead so the part seats flush.explanation: A part that stands off the board strains its joints every time the board flexes.
Form a lead so the part seats flush.practice: Bend the lead with pliers at the board thickness and let the part drop flush without pushing it.

Heat the pad and lead together before fe.criterion: The joint reaches temperature first; solder follows the heat.
Heat the pad and lead together before fe.explanation: Solder fed onto the tip makes a cold joint that looks finished and fails later.
Heat the pad and lead together before fe.practice: Touch the tip to the pad and the lead at once, count two seconds, then feed solder into the joint, not the tip.

Insert a part in the right orientation.check_prompt: Which feature decides the part's orientation?
Insert a part in the right orientation.criterion: The part's marking and the board's marking face the same way.
Insert a part in the right orientation.explanation: Orientation errors survive soldering and only show up when the circuit does not work.
Insert a part in the right orientation.intent: Teach polarity against the board marking.
Insert a part in the right orientation.practice: Find the marking on the part and match it to the board's own marking before you bend anything.

Inspect a finished joint against the fil.criterion: A sound joint is shiny, concave and covers the pad without a ball.
Inspect a finished joint against the fil.explanation: Applying one criterion to many joints is the skill; the criterion itself does not change.
Inspect a finished joint against the fil.intent: Apply the criterion to a real joint.
Inspect a finished joint against the fil.practice: Judge each joint on the board against the fillet criterion and mark the ones that need rework.

Inspect a pad for lift before inserting.check_prompt: What does a lifted pad do under light pressure?
Inspect a pad for lift before inserting.criterion: A sound pad sits flat on the board; a lifted pad shows a shadow line and gives under light pressure.
Inspect a pad for lift before inserting.explanation: A lifted pad turns a one-minute joint into a board repair, so it is checked before heat.
Inspect a pad for lift before inserting.practice: Look at the pad edge against the board and press gently with a toothpick before you insert anything.

Name the three burn and fume hazards at.check_prompt: Which hazard do solder fumes mainly create?
Name the three burn and fume hazards at.criterion: The three hazards are the hot iron, the solder fumes and flying clippings near the eyes.
Name the three burn and fume hazards at.explanation: Naming the hazard is what makes the bench rules stick when you are concentrating on the joint.
Name the three burn and fume hazards at.intent: Name the hazards before touching the iron.
Name the three burn and fume hazards at.practice: Point at the iron, the fume path and your eyes, and name the hazard each one creates.

Prove continuity with a meter after rewo.check_prompt: Which meter setting proves the repair conducts?
Prove continuity with a meter after rewo.criterion: Continuity between the intended points proves the repair conducts.
Prove continuity with a meter after rewo.explanation: A joint can look right and still be open; the meter is the check the eye cannot make.
Prove continuity with a meter after rewo.practice: Set the meter to continuity, probe the two ends of the repaired path, and confirm the beep before power.

Read a resistor value from its colour ba.criterion: Brown, black, red, gold is ten times one hundred, so one thousand ohms at five percent.
Read a resistor value from its colour ba.explanation: The code is positional, so reading order matters more than colour memory.
Read a resistor value from its colour ba.practice: Read the bands left to right, then multiply by the third band before you trust the value.

Recognise a cold joint from its surface.check_prompt: What does a cold joint look like?
Recognise a cold joint from its surface.criterion: A cold joint has a grainy, matte surface; a sound fillet is bright and concave.
Recognise a cold joint from its surface.explanation: Surface is the cheapest inspection you have, and it is read before power is applied.
Recognise a cold joint from its surface.practice: Compare a grainy joint with a bright fillet and say which one moved while it cooled.

Set an iron to the temperature a leaded.check_prompt: What temperature range suits leaded solder?
Set an iron to the temperature a leaded.criterion: Leaded solder wants a moderate setting; hotter burns the flux before the joint forms.
Set an iron to the temperature a leaded.explanation: Temperature is a time control: too cold means a longer touch and a colder joint.
Set an iron to the temperature a leaded.intent: Teach the temperature setting for leaded solder.
Set an iron to the temperature a leaded.practice: Set the station, wait for the display to settle, and tin the tip before the first joint.

Wick a solder bridge without lifting the.check_prompt: When do you lift the wick?
Wick a solder bridge without lifting the.criterion: Heat through the wick and stop as soon as the bridge disappears.
Wick a solder bridge without lifting the.explanation: Pulling the wick while the solder is solid is how pads lift.
Wick a solder bridge without lifting the.practice: Add flux, lay the wick over the bridge, and heat the wick until the solder flows into it before lifting.
Wick a solder bridge without lifting the.reference_answer: after the solder flows into it
